metadata.description: Crude oil import ports, processing refineries, and key supply pipelines for Germany.
primary_sources: en2x – German Fuels and Energy Association (formerly MWV)

properties.name: Wilhelmshaven Oil Hub (NWO & JadeWeserPort)
properties.capacity: approx. 20 million tonnes of crude oil per year
properties.summary: Germany’s central crude oil import hub – the only deep-water port for VLCCs, where seaborne crude converges and is redistributed by pipeline.
properties.description: Wilhelmshaven is the single most important crude oil gateway into Germany. Around 80% of all seaborne crude imports enter here. Tankers arriving via the North Sea approach discharge at the oil pier; from this hub the Nord-West Oelleitung (NWO) and the Norddeutsche Oelleitung (NDO) redistribute the oil to refineries in western and northern Germany. Multiple inbound flows therefore meet at one node and then branch out again – a classic supply-chain hub.
consumer_products: Gasoline & diesel for northern and western Germany
Petrochemical feedstocks for plastics and chemicals

aha_moment.title: Where the oil streams meet
aha_moment.explanation: Seaborne crude from the North Sea and global trades arrives at Wilhelmshaven. From this single pier the oil is split into major pipeline corridors: NWO toward the Rhine (Shell Rheinland and beyond) and NDO toward Hamburg. One import point feeds several refining regions.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: A large share of the fuel used in Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia and Hamburg has passed through this hub before reaching a refinery and finally a filling station.

properties.name: Rostock Oil Port
properties.summary: Strategic Baltic Sea import port supplying eastern Germany.
properties.description: Since deliveries through Russia’s Druzhba pipeline stopped, the port of Rostock has become the vital supply artery for the PCK refinery in Schwedt. Tankers from Norway, North America and West Africa discharge here.
consumer_products: Jet fuel for Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER)

aha_moment.title: A Baltic lifeline instead of Druzhba
aha_moment.explanation: Within a very short time, Rostock was turned from a regional terminal into a geopolitical key axis for the energy security of Germany’s capital region.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Secures the fuel supply for emergency services, buses and cars in Berlin and Brandenburg.

source.name: German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK)

properties.name: Port of Trieste (SIOT Marine Terminal, Italy)
properties.capacity: approx. 43 million tonnes of crude oil / year
properties.summary: Southern gateway for crude oil to Bavaria, Baden-Württemberg and Central Europe.
properties.description: Crude oil tankers from the Mediterranean, North Africa and the Middle East discharge in Trieste. From here, the Transalpine Pipeline (TAL) pumps the oil across the Alps directly to southern German refineries.
consumer_products: Heating oil for the Alpine region

aha_moment.title: Oil flows across the Alps
aha_moment.explanation: More than 90% of the crude oil in Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg does not come from the North Sea – it is pumped via Trieste and spectacular mountain tunnels right across Austria into Germany.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: The fuel for every car and truck on Bavaria’s motorways originally arrived on ships in the Adriatic.

properties.name: PCK Refinery Schwedt
properties.summary: The heart of the fuel supply for Berlin, Brandenburg and western Poland.
properties.description: The PCK refinery processes crude oil into high-purity fuels. It supplies around 95% of all filling stations in Berlin and Brandenburg as well as the capital’s BER airport directly by pipeline.
consumer_products: Diesel for public transport and haulage companies
Jet A-1 aviation fuel for BER

aha_moment.title: Every flight from Berlin flies on Schwedt
aha_moment.explanation: Almost every scheduled flight taking off from Berlin’s BER airport is fuelled with kerosene refined in Schwedt and pumped to Schönefeld through a dedicated direct pipeline.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Your holiday flight to Mallorca or your drive around the Berlin ring road is powered from here.

properties.name: TotalEnergies Refinery Central Germany (Leuna)
properties.summary: Germany’s most modern refinery and the energy supplier of central Germany.
properties.description: Leuna (Saxony-Anhalt) is home to one of the most advanced large refineries in Europe. It supplies around 1,300 filling stations in central Germany and delivers petrochemical feedstocks to the Leuna chemical site.

aha_moment.title: From crude oil to a box of aspirin
aha_moment.explanation: Leuna’s base materials are turned not only into fuels but also into precursors for plastics, insulation for house facades and pharmaceutical excipients.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Keeps Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia moving and supplies plastics for packaging.

properties.name: MiRO Upper Rhine Refinery (Karlsruhe)
properties.summary: Germany’s largest fuel refinery and a central pillar of the south-west.
properties.description: One in four litres of gasoline and diesel consumed in Germany comes from MiRO in Karlsruhe. It is fed mainly via the Transalpine Pipeline (TAL) from Trieste.
consumer_products: Propylene for automotive and electronic components

aha_moment.title: 25% of all car journeys in Germany
aha_moment.explanation: Statistically, one in four tank fills anywhere in Germany comes from the distillation towers on the banks of the Rhine in Karlsruhe.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Powers cars, trucks and farm machinery throughout Baden-Württemberg, Rhineland-Palatinate and Hesse.

properties.name: Shell Energy and Chemicals Park Rheinland (Cologne/Wesseling)
properties.capacity: approx. 17 million tonnes / year (incl. chemical complex)
properties.summary: Germany’s largest integrated refinery and chemicals complex.
properties.description: The Wesseling and Godorf sites are connected directly by pipeline to Rotterdam and Wilhelmshaven. Among others, they supply Frankfurt and Cologne/Bonn airports with kerosene.
consumer_products: Base chemicals for the pharmaceutical industry

aha_moment.title: Fuel for Europe’s biggest aviation hub
aha_moment.explanation: Frankfurt Airport uses enormous amounts of kerosene. Much of it is produced in Wesseling and travels through underground pipelines, without truck traffic, straight to the aircraft stands.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Enables worldwide cargo and passenger traffic from Frankfurt am Main.

properties.name: BP Refinery Gelsenkirchen (Horst & Scholven)
properties.operator: Ruhr Oel GmbH / BP Europa SE
properties.summary: Petrochemical powerhouse in the heart of the Ruhr area.
properties.description: Closely integrated into the north-west European pipeline network. Besides fuels, it produces feedstocks for the entire chemical industry of the Ruhr area.

aha_moment.title: From crude oil to smartphone casing
aha_moment.explanation: Naphtha delivered from Wilhelmshaven is cracked into ethylene here – the basis for polyethylene, used in modern smartphone displays, cable insulation and medical products.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Without this petrochemistry there would be no modern screens, lightweight cars or sterile packaging.

properties.name: Bayernoil Refinery (Vohburg & Neustadt an der Donau)
properties.summary: Central energy source for Bavaria and parts of Austria.
properties.description: Supplied via the TAL pipeline from Trieste. Produces fuels for the Bavarian market and supplies the Bavarian Chemical Triangle (Burghausen).

aha_moment.title: The engine of the south
aha_moment.explanation: Munich Airport is supplied with jet fuel directly from Bayernoil and Burghausen. Bavaria’s industry also relies on their process heat and base materials.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Secures heat and mobility for millions of people in the Free State of Bavaria.

properties.name: BP Refinery Lingen (Emsland)
properties.summary: Specialised refinery and pioneer in green hydrogen and co-processing.
properties.description: Supplied via the NWO pipeline from Wilhelmshaven. Lingen is taking a pioneering role today by increasingly combining fossil crude oil with biogenic residues and green hydrogen to make sustainable aviation fuel (SAF).

aha_moment.title: The bridge to the future
aha_moment.explanation: Here, traditional crude oil processing meets Germany’s largest industrial electrolysers for green hydrogen.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Shows how the transition from fossil infrastructure to renewable e-fuels is actually taking place.

properties.name: Holborn Europa Refinery (Hamburg-Harburg)
properties.summary: Supplier for the Hamburg metropolitan region and Schleswig-Holstein.
properties.description: Receives crude oil via the NDO pipeline from Wilhelmshaven. Supplies the Port of Hamburg, the maritime economy and local public transport.
consumer_products: Marine diesel for the Port of Hamburg

aha_moment.title: Fuel for Europe’s third-largest port
aha_moment.explanation: Tugboats, harbour ferries and truck fleets in the Port of Hamburg run on fuels produced just a few kilometres south of the Elbe.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Keeps the movement of goods in northern Germany going.

properties.name: North-West Oil Pipeline (NWO)
properties.flow_direction: Wilhelmshaven Oil Hub → Shell Rheinland (Cologne/Wesseling) and western Germany
properties.summary: Main outbound pipeline from the Wilhelmshaven oil hub to the Rhine refinery cluster.
properties.description: The Nord-West Oelleitung is the primary artery leaving the Wilhelmshaven hub. It carries crude that has just been unloaded from tankers southward to the large refining and chemical complex in the Rhine area (Shell Energy and Chemicals Park Rheinland).
consumer_products: Crude oil feed for refineries in the west

aha_moment.title: Invisible beneath meadows and fields
aha_moment.explanation: With a diameter of 70 centimetres, the NWO pumps enormous volumes of crude oil around the clock without drivers on the motorways or walkers in the fields ever noticing.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Replaces thousands of truck journeys or rail tank cars every day.

properties.name: North German Oil Pipeline (NDO)
properties.flow_direction: Wilhelmshaven Oil Hub → Holborn Europa Refinery (Hamburg)
properties.summary: Outbound pipeline from the Wilhelmshaven oil hub to the Hamburg refining area.
properties.description: The Norddeutsche Oelleitung leaves the Wilhelmshaven hub eastward and supplies the Holborn Europa refinery in Hamburg-Harburg. Together with the NWO it shows how one import hub feeds multiple regions.
consumer_products: Crude oil feed for Hamburg & northern Germany

aha_moment.title: Oil flows under the Weser
aha_moment.explanation: The pipeline crosses deep beneath the bed of the Weser river and supplies Hamburg with crude oil without adding to shipping traffic on the Elbe.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Secures the fuel supply for shipping and the airport in Hamburg.

properties.name: Pipeline Rostock – Schwedt
properties.operator: PCK Raffinerie GmbH / German federal government
properties.summary: Strategic supply line from the Baltic coast to the Uckermark region.
properties.description: Has replaced deliveries through the Druzhba pipeline since 2023. The German federal government is funding a technical upgrade with drag-reducing agents to increase capacity.

aha_moment.title: From side track to main artery
aha_moment.explanation: Originally intended only as an emergency backup line, this pipeline now carries the vital oil for eastern Germany’s entire capital region.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Keeps Berlin’s public transport and emergency services on the road.

source.name: BMWK press release on the PCK upgrade

properties.name: Transalpine Pipeline (TAL)
properties.operator: TAL Group (Società Italiana per l'Oleodotto Transalpino / Transalpine Ölleitung in Österreich / Deutsche Transalpine Oelleitung)
properties.summary: A European engineering masterpiece across the Alps.
properties.description: Runs from Trieste through Italy, crosses the Alps in Carinthia and Salzburg in tunnels at up to 1,572 metres above sea level, and reaches the refinery centre in Bavaria.
consumer_products: Crude oil for Bavaria, Baden-Württemberg, Austria & Czechia

aha_moment.title: Oil in an Alpine tunnel at 1,500 m
aha_moment.explanation: To get the crude oil over the Alps, giant high-pressure pumps push it through the Felbertauern tunnel – a 7.3 km mountain tunnel built just for oil.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Supplies 100% of Bavaria’s and about 50% of Baden-Württemberg’s crude oil.

properties.name: Rhine-Danube Oil Pipeline (TAL-West / RDO)
properties.summary: Western branch of the TAL from Bavaria to Baden-Württemberg.
properties.description: Carries crude oil from the Transalpine Pipeline from Ingolstadt via Schwäbisch Gmünd directly to the large MiRO refinery on the Rhine in Karlsruhe.
consumer_products: Crude oil supply for south-west Germany

aha_moment.title: The southern cross-link
aha_moment.explanation: Connects the Danube and the Rhine underground and supplies Germany’s largest refinery with Mediterranean crude oil.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Makes Baden-Württemberg’s crude supply independent of low water levels for Rhine shipping.

properties.name: North Sea Tanker Route
properties.flow_direction: Strait of Dover → Dutch and German coast → Wilhelmshaven Oil Hub
properties.summary: Inbound tanker approach into Germany’s central crude oil hub at Wilhelmshaven.
properties.description: This shipping corridor represents the final inbound leg of crude oil tankers heading for Wilhelmshaven – Germany’s only deep-water oil port. All of this flow converges on the oil pier before being redistributed by the NWO and NDO pipelines.

aha_moment.title: In the wake of supertankers
aha_moment.explanation: Ships with up to 250,000 tonnes deadweight and 20 metres draught can only berth here. Nowhere else on Germany’s coast is the sea deep enough.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Connects Germany to the world’s oil markets.

source.name: German Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration (WSV)

properties.name: Adriatic Tanker Route to Trieste
properties.summary: Mediterranean shipping corridor for crude oil imports to Central Europe.
properties.description: Carries crude oil from the Middle East, Central Asia (via the Bosporus / Caspian Sea) and North Africa through the Ionian Sea and the Adriatic to Trieste.
consumer_products: Crude oil imports for southern Germany & the Alpine region

aha_moment.title: The Silk Road of liquid gold
aha_moment.explanation: Through this sea route, crude oil from the major producing regions of the Middle East flows directly to Trieste and ends up as gasoline in car tanks in Munich or Stuttgart.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Connects German drivers with global trade routes spanning thousands of nautical miles.

source.name: SIOT / Port of Trieste traffic report

properties.name: Eastern Mediterranean Tanker Approach (Suez)
properties.operator: Various (Libya, Egypt, Middle East via Suez)
properties.capacity: Multiple loading ports feeding the Adriatic route
properties.summary: Shipping approach where crude tankers from the Gulf (via Suez) and North Africa converge on the route to Trieste.
properties.description: Crude oil arriving at the SIOT terminal in Trieste comes from several Mediterranean and Middle Eastern loading regions. This node represents the collective eastern-Mediterranean / Suez approach where tankers enter the route toward the Adriatic and the Transalpine Pipeline (TAL) system.

aha_moment.title: From the Mediterranean to your tank
aha_moment.explanation: Tankers load crude in North Africa and the Middle East, pass through the eastern Mediterranean, and discharge at Trieste. From there the TAL pipeline carries the oil into southern Germany and Austria.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: A significant share of diesel and gasoline used in southern Germany has travelled this Mediterranean–Adriatic–TAL route.

properties.name: Strait of Dover (English Channel Approach)
properties.capacity: One of the busiest shipping lanes in the world
properties.summary: Shipping approach where tankers from the Atlantic leave the English Channel for the final leg along the Dutch and German coast to Wilhelmshaven.
properties.description: Tankers from the US Gulf Coast, Venezuela and Canada cross the Atlantic, pass Brittany and run up the English Channel. At the Strait of Dover – only about 33 km wide – they enter the North Sea and follow the Dutch and German coast to Wilhelmshaven, Germany’s only deep-water oil port. Crude from North Sea fields reaches the port directly from the north and is not yet shown on the map.

aha_moment.title: Through the English Channel
aha_moment.explanation: Loaded supertankers bound for Wilhelmshaven share the Strait of Dover with ferries, container ships and fishing boats. Traffic runs in separate one-way lanes, like a motorway at sea.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Much of the fuel used in northern and western Germany has passed the Strait of Dover on its way to the Wilhelmshaven oil pier.

properties.flow_direction: Atlantic trades → English Channel → Strait of Dover → Wilhelmshaven Oil Hub
